- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast by 5–15% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a high, model frequently fails to adjust; add lagged mean reversion rule: if 3-day moving avg of true values drops below 10% of prior peak, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., -0.3 to 0.3), model often overfits recent volatility; use 30-day smoothed historical mean as baseline anchor.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 14-day moving average of history, apply bias correction: if true is lower, forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for suppressed volatility.
